decision_question: Is there primary evidence that isolates which historical checkpoint/rewind target should be selected while holding alarm/trigger, available candidate checkpoints, carry-forward state, model, task set, harness and budget fixed?

final_outcomes_required: false-positive disruption or unsafe-effect cost where applicable

scoped_primary_search_result.scope_note: This is an absence result only for the primary literature and source surfaces searched in this invocation as of 2026-08-26. It is not a proof that no qualifying study exists anywhere.
scoped_primary_search_result.material_conclusion: The quality of historical restore-target selection remains causally unidentified by the closest agent recovery studies reviewed. Do not promote looser rollback, depth, trigger, checkpoint-semantics or carry-forward ablations as selector-only evidence.

near_matches.study: AgentRewind: Rewinding Tool-Using Agents to Recover from Failures
near_matches.what_is_controlled: A paired recovery study begins from the same failed endpoints with the same GPT-5.4 mini-SWE-agent configuration, deterministic temperature, starting context/workspace and termination conditions. Rewind exposes a bounded historical candidate set (up to 80 checkpoints) and retained rewind memory.
near_matches.what_is_missing: No selector-policy ablation compares model-selected target against immediate predecessor, fixed depth, latest-known-good, dependency/root-cause/admissibility-constrained or random target while preserving the same candidate set. The component ablation changes environment rewind, context rewind and rewind memory while explicitly leaving checkpoint selection unchanged.
near_matches.qualification: closest matched recovery substrate, but not a selector-only factorial

near_matches.study: ReAgent: Reversible Multi-Agent Reasoning for Knowledge-Enhanced Multi-Hop QA
near_matches.what_is_controlled: The paper studies local backtracking and reports a local backtracking-depth sensitivity under otherwise matched benchmark/model settings.
near_matches.what_is_missing: Changing allowed backtracking depth changes which historical nodes are reachable. It therefore changes the candidate set/reach rather than holding candidates fixed and changing only the selector policy.

near_matches.study: WebRollback: Learning When and Where to Roll Back in Web Agents
near_matches.what_is_controlled: The rollback module can inspect prior states and select an earlier state index.
near_matches.what_is_missing: The main OneWay/BestFirst/Rollback comparison changes search/control behavior and rollback triggering as well as where to resume. It does not isolate target selection under a fixed alarm and identical candidates/carry-forward/budget.
near_matches.qualification: when-and-where policy comparison, not selector-only factorial

near_matches.study: DART: Semantic Recoverability for Structured Tool Agents
near_matches.what_is_controlled: DART selects the latest admissible semantic checkpoint and compares against retry/coarse/entry-oriented recovery baselines.
near_matches.what_is_missing: The compared methods alter admissibility, checkpoint semantics, candidate spaces and/or whole-task retry behavior. The restore-target selector is not the sole changed factor.
near_matches.qualification: strong checkpoint/admissibility evidence, but selector causality remains confounded

near_matches.study: Generator-Assistant Stepwise Rollback Framework for Large Language Model Agent
near_matches.what_is_controlled: Wait-Info varies how much post-error information the assistant sees before rollback localization and exhibits a non-monotonic optimum.
near_matches.what_is_missing: This changes diagnosis information horizon, not the target selector over a fixed historical candidate set.

not_supported: claiming agent-selected rewind is better than fixed-depth or latest-known-good selection
claiming deeper rollback is better because of selector quality rather than candidate reach
claiming rollback-policy gains isolate historical target choice when trigger/carry-forward/checkpoint semantics also change
negative_scope_guard.supported: A strict selector-only causal comparison remains a high-value verification gap.

recommended_positive_control.purpose: Resolve selector causality without changing the recovery substrate.
recommended_positive_control.design: Use the same paired failed endpoints and freeze the alarm/trigger, ordered candidate checkpoint list, checkpoint payloads, retained memory/carry-forward, model, decoding, task set, evaluator, step/token/wall-clock budget and termination. Randomize only the selector among model-choice, immediate predecessor, fixed depth, latest-known-good, dependency/root-cause or semantic-admissibility constrained, and random candidate. Report final success/progress, recovery attempts, tokens, wall-clock and effect/disruption cost.
recommended_positive_control.status: proposed verification control; not source evidence
